To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the phytomass of shrub ecosystems in the study region was 1143 g/m 2 for heathland, 447 g/m 2 in rock rose thicket – heathland, and 788 g/m 2 rock rose thicket, and 1404g/m 2 in gorse thicket, 695g/m 2 for mancha bushland and 1966g/m 2 of Pistacia lentiscsus bushland.
we have shown that the above-ground phitomass of the studied shrubs is 1,143 g m –2, with a mean photosynthetic-to- total phitomass ratio of 0.19.

the above-ground phitomas of shrub formations in the southern Iberian Peninsula is highly variable, ranging from 447 to 1966 g/m², and that carbon sequestered by the above-ground phitomass ranged from 2.23 to 9.8 t C ha-1, depending on the shrub formation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the estimation of biomass in Mediterranean scrub ecosystems.
the development of a methodology for estimating the biomass and carbon pool of the shrub ecosystems in southern Spain.
the estimation of above-ground phytomas and carbon pool in Mediterranean woody shrubland ecosystems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Mediterranean shrub ecosystems of Southern Spain are important reservoirs of sequestered biomass carbon.
the Mediterranean shrubland ecosystems in southern Spain sequester 4–10 t ha –1 of carbon, and that the photosynthetic biomass represents approximately 20% of the total phytomass.

the above-ground phitomas estimates obtained for shrubs and bushes in southern Spain were 1143 and 1404 kg ha –1 for heath and gorse thicket, respectively, and 695 and 1966 kg ha –1, for mancha high-bush and Pistacia lentiscu, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Mediterranean shrub ecosystems of the Iberian Peninsula sequester a mean value of approximately 6 t C ha –1.

we have shown that it is possible to estimate the above-ground phytic biomass in shrub ecosystems of Southern Spain, and that this biomass is comparable to that of forests in terms of the amount of carbon stored.
, in general, shrubs have a higher biomass than heath and rock rose thicket communities and, in turn, the latter have higher values than the mancha bush formations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
shrubs are an important component of the carbon budget in Mediterranean ecosystems.
the carbon sequestration capacity of the shrublands of Southern Spain is comparable to that of other Mediterranean shrublands, but is lower than the carbon sequestrations in the forests.
the carbon pool of shrubs in Mediterranean ecosystems is higher than previously thought.
